_comment: Known GGUF candidates. Every url and size was read from the HuggingFace API and HEAD-checked. Reference it from bench.json as {"use": "<name>"}.

ships-mid.label: Fits a mid/high tier phone (<= 1.0 GB)

borderline.label: Over the phone budget, close enough to be tempting

lab.label: PC only - answers 'does size fix it?'

lfm2-350m.note: Looked fine on 9 words and collapsed on 101 (18/101 baseline, 67/101 shaped). Too small - the 9-word result was noise.

lfm2-700m.note: SHIPPING TODAY. 94/101 meaning, 89/101 exact on the shaped prompt - good, but LFM2-1.2B is perfect for 0.24 GB more.

qwen2.5-0.5b.note: Erratic: 4-7/9 primary across prompts. Invents confident alternatives when given room.

qwen3-0.6b.note: Tested: 8/9 primary, 1/7 second, and it loops - 'das Haus' -> a house, a house in the house, a house in the house's house.

smollm2-360m.note: Weakest of the set: 4-7/9 primary depending on prompt. A floor to measure against, not a candidate.

granite-350m.note: NOT broken after all: a long prompt silences it (9/9 empty), a one-sentence prompt gets 7/9. The prompt was the bug, not the model.

lfm2-1.2b.note: BEST TRANSLATOR OF ALL 13. Perfect 101/101 meaning, article and exact form on the shaped prompt. No alternatives (0/7), but nothing has those.

llama3.2-1b.note: Very prompt-sensitive: 5/9 primary on a long prompt, 8/9 on a one-sentence one, with fabrication dropping to zero.

gemma3-1b.note: The most willing to list (2/7 on a verbose prompt) - but it fabricated on both controls in every variant that found anything.

qwen2.5-1.5b.note: Superb on a plain prompt (100/101) and collapses to 37/101 when asked to shape the output. Prompt-coupled - do not swap prompts under it.

eurollm-1.7b.note: The steadiest: 9/9 primary on four of five prompts, zero fabrication throughout, and 0/7 second meanings under every one.

smollm2-1.7b.note: Quietly strong: 9/9 primary on short prompts, never fabricates. Never lists a second meaning either.

qwen3-1.7b.note: Reasoning-tuned; sweep.ps1 already disables thinking for it. The largest Qwen3 worth trying before the size jump.

salamandra-2b.note: EU-funded, trained across all official EU languages. Unusual German depth per parameter - the dark horse here.

lfm2-2.6b.note: Top of the LFM2 line. Answers whether the family scales, even though ~8.8 GB of RAM puts it out of phone reach.

gemma2-2b.note: Older, but punches above its size. Over budget on a 7.5 GB phone once the vision model is also installed.

qwen2.5-3b.note: First rung where general knowledge gets real. The 'does 3B fix it' test.

llama3.2-3b.note: Same family and tuning as llama3.2-1b, so it is the cleanest A/B for size alone. Run this pair together.

smollm3-3b.note: Fully open 3B with real multilingual training, German included.

phi3.5-mini.note: Excellent instruction-following, thinner multilingual. Good for separating 'won't' from 'can't'.

gemma3-4b.note: Where Gemma 3's multilingual support officially begins - the honest comparison against gemma3-1b.

qwen3-4b.note: Strong for its size; same no-think caveat as qwen3-1.7b.

qwen2.5-7b.note: THE decider. If 7B still fabricates on single-meaning words, alternatives are a cloud feature regardless of hardware.

qwen3-8b.note: Newer generation at the same size, for a second opinion at the top of the ladder.

llama3.1-8b.note: Completes the Llama ladder: 1B -> 3B -> 8B on identical tuning.

ministral-8b.note: Mistral's small model, solid on European languages.

tower-7b.note: Purpose-built for translation (Unbabel). Best case for raw quality - but likely shares EuroLLM's refusal to do anything but translate.

occiglot-de-7b.note: German-English bilingual continued pretraining. The most on-point specialist in the list for exactly our task.

discolm-de-7b.note: German-native fine-tune on a Mistral-7B base. Old now, but genuinely German rather than German-capable.

eurollm-9b.note: The 1.7B we tested, scaled up. Directly answers whether that refusal-to-list behaviour is the tuning or the size.

teuken-7b.note: German/EU public-funded model. RESEARCH LICENCE - check the terms before shipping anything based on it.
